entities.summary: Pietro Riario was an Italian cardinal and Papal diplomat who played a pivotal role in shaping the papacy's diplomatic relations with European monarchs during the late Middle Ages. Born into the noble Riario family, Pietro rose through the ranks of the Catholic Church, becoming Cardinal in 1447. He served as Secretary to Pope Sixtus IV and later as Papal Legate to France, negotiating key alliances between the Holy See and French monarchs. Riario's diplomatic efforts helped establish a fragile peace during the tumultuous Italian Wars. His legacy can be seen in the continued influence of the papacy on European politics, particularly in the realm of ecclesiastical diplomacy.
